app/server.mjs:238,310,496 — only core htmx attributes (hx-get/target/swap/push-url/trigger/sync), stable since htmx 1.x

reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview, RC, or canary APIs; the whole app runs on the framework's most boring, most documented surface, pinned to current stable versions.

evidence: app/lib/api.mjs:1-2 — all HTTP access isolated in one thin client module, itself only using global fetch and Node built-ins
app/scripts/build.mjs:1-9 — build step is a plain fs copyFile of htmx dist, no bundler flags

evidence: app/server.mjs:809 — serve() is the only supported way to run Hono on Node; @hono/node-server v2 release notes confirm the public API is unchanged from v1 (github.com/honojs/node-server/releases/tag/v2.0.0)
app/server.mjs:33-35 — interactivity uses HX-Request header + partial HTML responses, the standard htmx pattern with no extensions or client JS

justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all; each stable API chosen is the minimal canonical option (node adapter, html templates, core htmx attributes) rather than a novel one.

findings.issue: @hono/node-server is pinned to 2.x, a major released ~6 months ago (2026-04-21), so it is the newest dependency in the tree.
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change: the v2 release notes state the public API is identical to v1, so migration risk is negligible; keep monitoring release notes for the 1.x→2.x line as usual.

summary: This app is maximally conservative on the experimentalness axis: every line runs on long-stable core APIs of Hono, the official Node adapter, and vanilla htmx, with zero experimental markers, flags, or preview versions. The only recent-stable dependency is @hono/node-server 2.x, whose public API is unchanged from v1. Framework-churn risk is essentially zero.
